project_objective_text: To clean and organise district-level weekly disease-outbreak data for Maharashtra from official surveillance sources.
evidence_produced: Reconstructed 809-row master analytical dataset (2022-2026 W32) from primary NCDC weekly outbreak PDFs; 539 baseline records across 5 primary families; complete audit of 49 raw disease labels mapped into 30 standardized families.
analytical_result: Established a fully auditable, clean secondary surveillance dataset with 100% provenance tracing to official government PDF archives.
methodological_limitation: Surveillance data capture outbreak events meeting threshold definitions, not total population morbidity; 2023 archive lacks published reports for W15, W51, W52.

project_objective_text: To analyse the monthly and annual distribution of reported disease-outbreak records during the 2022-2025 baseline period.
evidence_produced: Generated comprehensive monthly distribution registers, annual totals, and weekly distribution registers across 48 calendar months and 5 primary disease families.
analytical_result: Demonstrated distinct temporal distributions: Dengue concentrated in Jun-Oct (82.8%); Malaria in May-Jul (51.4%); ADD in Jun-Aug (43.1%); Food Poisoning bimodal in Jan-Feb & Apr-May (55.1%); Chikungunya diffuse.
methodological_limitation: Annual distributions subject to dominant-year surveillance surges (e.g., Dengue 2023: 51.0% of events; ADD 2024: 46.4% of events).

project_objective_text: To identify months with higher concentrations of reported outbreak cases and records using quantitative concentration metrics.
evidence_produced: Computed Coefficient of Variation (CV), Top-3 Concentration Ratio (CR3), Normalized Shannon Entropy, and Gini Coefficients for both reported events and cases across all 5 families.
analytical_result: Classified Dengue (CV=0.736, CR3=50.5%) and Malaria (CV=0.753, CR3=51.4%) as High Concentration; ADD (CV=0.524, CR3=43.1%) and Food Poisoning (CV=0.564, CR3=44.9%) as Moderate; Chikungunya as Diffuse (CV=0.515, CR3=39.5%).
methodological_limitation: Case concentration metrics are vulnerable to distortion by single high-case outbreak records (Food Poisoning Case CV=1.160; ADD Case CV=0.609).

project_objective_text: To compare the seasonal profiles, peak windows, and inter-annual stability of the selected diseases.
evidence_produced: Identified 3-month peak windows; evaluated contiguous vs discrete windows; performed Kendall's W concordance across annual rank profiles; tracked maximum peak month displacements.
analytical_result: Identified contiguous windows for Malaria (May-Jul) and ADD (Jun-Aug); discrete high-activity months for Dengue (Oct, Sep, Jun) and Food Poisoning (May, Feb, Jan); ADD showed highest rank concordance (W=0.530), Dengue moderate (W=0.405), Chikungunya lowest (W=0.150).
methodological_limitation: Kendall's W evaluates only 4 annual profile vectors, rendering p-values exploratory; does not assess meteorological causation.

project_objective_text: To examine district-level coverage and geographic variation in the reported outbreak data.
evidence_produced: Analyzed district-level event shares and peak reported-event months for all districts meeting academic sample threshold (N >= 10); computed Jun-Sep seasonal proportions for 13 qualifying district cohorts.
analytical_result: Revealed extreme spatial concentration for Malaria (Gadchiroli & Chandrapur = 61.4% of events) and Chikungunya (Pune = 25.6%); in contrast, Dengue and ADD showed broad statewide reporting across >30 districts.
methodological_limitation: Reflects spatial distribution of surveillance reporting and health facility notification density rather than true geographic incidence in the general population.

project_objective_text: To evaluate outlier sensitivity and event-case divergence in reported surveillance metrics.
evidence_produced: Conducted systematic outlier sensitivity testing by recomputing peak months and shares after excluding influential records; analyzed monthly event-to-case ratios.
analytical_result: Found Food Poisoning February case volume is strongly influenced by 3 high-case outbreak records (1,615 cases; peak shifts to April upon removal); ADD February case peak driven by 1 institutional outbreak (1,000 cases; peak shifts to Oct/Aug); Dengue is completely resilient.
methodological_limitation: Removing influential records reveals mathematical sensitivity of surveillance aggregates but does not invalidate the reality of the reported historical outbreaks.

project_objective_text: To conduct out-of-sample validation using partial-year 2026 data without invalid forecasting.
evidence_produced: Compared 2026 W01-W32 (45 records) against historical equivalent 4-year means; assessed variance, truncation vulnerability, and administrative label shifts.
analytical_result: ADD (18 events) matched historical mean (21.8); Dengue (6 events) showed severe truncation caveat (55.4% of events occur post-W32); Food Poisoning recorded 19 reported events in 2026 W01-W32 while all 19 records used the "Suspected Food Poisoning" label; Malaria (-91.7%) showed marked surveillance deficit.
methodological_limitation: 2026 is partial-year (32 weeks); cannot be compared to complete calendar years; cannot forecast unobserved W33-W52 activity.

project_objective_text: To formulate evidence-based conclusions for seasonal surveillance preparedness while recognizing the boundaries of outbreak-based data.
evidence_produced: Synthesized cross-phase evidence into formal evidence classifications (A/B/C/D); explicitly delineated supported findings from unsupported claims (causation, incidence, risk ranking).
analytical_result: Established that Dengue (Strong) and Malaria/ADD (Moderate) exhibit actionable seasonal timing patterns in surveillance reporting, while Food Poisoning is point-source driven and Chikungunya is data-sparse; defined 9 explicit unsupported claims for viva defense.
methodological_limitation: Conclusions apply strictly to public health outbreak surveillance logistics and preparedness, not clinical etiology, pathogen biology, or individual risk prediction.
